claims.statement: Meta documents an App Access Token that lets an app read and modify app settings and is generated server-to-server from the app ID and app secret.

sources.supports: App access tokens let you read and modify app settings. Generate one using your Meta app secret via a server-to-server call.
sources.locator: Access Tokens for Meta Technologies, App Access Tokens

claims.statement: Meta documents generating an app access token with a server-side GET to https://graph.facebook.com/oauth/access_token using the app ID as client_id, the app secret as client_secret and grant_type client_credentials, and states the call returns an app access token to use in place of a user access token; it states the request uses the app secret and must only be made by server-side code.

claims.statement: Meta documents, as another method that does not require a generated app access token, passing the app ID and the app secret joined by a pipe as the access_token parameter of a Graph API call, and says the choice between that method and a generated token depends on where the app secret is kept.

sources.supports: There is another method to make calls to the Graph API that doesn't require using a generated app access token. You can just pass your app ID and app secret as the access_token parameter when you make a call

claims.statement: Meta states that hard-coding an app access token in client-side code or app binaries exposes the app secret and gives anyone full access to modify the app, that app access tokens are for server-to-server calls only, and (on the Login Security page) that the App Secret or an App Access token should never be included in any code.

sources.supports: Never hard-code app access tokens into client-side code or app binaries — doing so exposes your app secret and gives anyone who loads your webpage or decompiles your app full access to modify it.
sources.locator: App Access Tokens, Generating an app access token

sources.supports: Therefore the App Secret or an App Access token should never be included in any code.

claims.statement: Meta states that for an app whose App Type is Native/Desktop it assumes the binary contains the App Secret or an App Access Token and does not allow calls signed with an App Access Token to proceed; the access-tokens page adds that app access tokens are insecure for such apps because the app secret is typically embedded in the code.

sources.supports: we assume that your native app contains the App Secret or an App Access Token in the binary, and we do not allow calls signed with an App Access Token to proceed
App access tokens are insecure if your app is set to `Native/Desktop` in the Advanced settings of your [App Dashboard](https://developers.facebook.com/apps).

sources.supports: Because client tokens are embedded in apps, they are not secret.

claims.statement: Meta documents appsecret_proof as a sha256 hash of an access token using the app secret as the key, computed with hash_hmac and added as a parameter to server-to-server Graph API calls; it is an output derived from the app secret and a token.

sources.supports: The app secret proof is a sha256 hash of your access token, using your app secret as the key.
sources.locator: Verify Graph API Calls with appsecret_proof

sources.supports: The app secret proof is a sha256 hash of your access token, using your app secret as the key.

claims.statement: Meta states that the length of access tokens changes over time as Meta updates what they store and how they are encoded, and advises a variable-length data type without a specific maximum size; the page gives no grammar for any token type including the app access token.

sources.supports: The length of access tokens changes over time as Meta updates what they store and how they are encoded.

claims.statement: Meta states that when a Meta app is created it is assigned a unique ID, which must be included when making calls to its APIs, and that the Basic Settings page is where the app secret assigned by Meta is found.

sources.supports: When you create a Facebook app we generate and assign it a unique ID. This ID must be included when making any calls to our APIs.

openQuestions.question: Only existence is established. The access-tokens page states that token length changes over time and gives no format grammar; it is not recorded here.

The same page documents passing the app ID and app secret joined by a pipe as the access_token parameter instead of a generated token. Whether that composite is one more form of this family, a form of meta:app-secret, or neither is not settled; no format claim is made.

Which family the pipe-joined app ID and app secret belongs to is not settled by the sources and is not forced here. Established: the second part is the app secret the page names, the page presents the form as an alternative to a generated app access token, and the same access_token parameter takes a generated token, the app-ID-and-secret pair and the app-ID-and-client-token pair. Whether Meta calls the pair an access token, and whether its privilege equals a generated token's, is not stated.

The page states that the generation call returns an app access token but shows no response body, so the member that carries it and its encoding are not stated on the pages read. Token length is stated to vary over time and no prefix or alphabet is given; no format is claimed.

Whether a generated app access token carries the same standing as the app secret it was generated from, or can be rotated independently of it, is not stated; the pages say only that exposing the token exposes the app secret and that the app secret cannot be rotated programmatically (recorded in the app-secret family).
